evidence.claim: Riverbend's 2025 annual report cites cardiac OR case volume down 9% YoY, attributed to staffing and room-turnover time.
Open job posts for two Cardiac Perfusionists and one CV Surgical First Assistant, unfilled for 90+ days.
Chief of Cardiac Surgery quoted in AHA regional panel: 'We can't accept every referral we're offered — throughput is our binding constraint.'
evidence.source: AHA Midwest Cardiac Summit panel recap, Feb 2026

evidence.claim: Peer institution (Mercy Heart, comparable size) published a case study in JTCVS showing 14% increase in weekly case volume after adopting a room-turnover optimization program.

symptoms: Cardiac case volume declined 9% YoY despite demand
Persistent unfilled perfusionist and CV first-assist roles
Public acknowledgment by the chief that throughput caps referrals
problem_diagnosis.likely_root_cause: Room turnover and staffing gaps are compounding — each unfilled role forces conservative scheduling, which depresses throughput more than the headcount gap alone would predict.
problem_diagnosis.cost_of_inaction: At an estimated contribution margin of $38k per cardiac case, the 9% volume decline represents ~$9.6M/yr in lost contribution at current mix.
problem_diagnosis.why_now: The fiscal year closes in June; the service line's FY27 capex request is being finalized in May and will lock in OR investment decisions for 24 months.

hypothesis.gap: Throughput ceiling set by turnover + staffing, not by demand or physical capacity.
hypothesis.desired_outcome: Restore case volume to pre-decline baseline without adding OR footprint, before the FY27 plan is locked.

readiness_signals: Public acknowledgment of the binding constraint
Peer institution has a published playbook for the same problem
Capex decision window closes in ~6 weeks
